about: A tool that turns Markdown files into a documentation website.

prs.title: Moving a site over from MkDocs gives a working sidebar
prs.broken: Importing an MkDocs site built a broken sidebar: some links went to pages that did not exist, plugin names showed up as menu items, and quoted titles kept their quotes.
prs.changed: The importer now reads only the menu section, links folder home pages correctly and drops the quotes.
prs.matters: People switching from MkDocs get a sidebar that works the first time.

prs.title: Sidebar links work on every page of a site moved from MkDocs
prs.broken: After moving a site over from MkDocs, sidebar and next/previous links on any page below the home page pointed to pages that did not exist.
prs.changed: Menu links from the import now start at the site root, so they lead to the same page from anywhere.
prs.matters: People switching from MkDocs get a site that can be browsed past the home page.

prs.title: VitePress migration copies pages in folders
prs.broken: Migrating a standard VitePress site copied only its top-level pages. Pages in folders and the public folder were left behind, while the tool still said the migration was complete.
prs.changed: Every folder of the site is now copied, except hidden ones.
prs.matters: Migrated sites keep all of their pages.

prs.title: VitePress migration finds TypeScript configs
prs.broken: Migrating a VitePress site set up with TypeScript stopped with a missing config error, because the tool did not look for config.mts.
prs.changed: The migration now also looks for config.mts.
prs.matters: TypeScript VitePress sites can be migrated.
